newsitem.title: COMOROS: Too short a skirt could mean jail in Comoros.
newsitem.headline: Too short a skirt could mean jail in Comoros.

text.p: The army chief-of-staff in the Comoro Islands warned local women and girls on Sunday that any of them caught wearing mini-skirts or tight-fitting dresses would be imprisoned by his troops.
"They must wear the veil," Muilim Djoussouf said on radio.
Djoussouff also warned men not to sport dreadlocks and not to wear necklaces or earrings on the Indian Ocean islands with their predominantly Moslem population.
He said the army would carry out sweeps this week and would arrest anyone ignoring his order. "They will remain in prison until they become healed," he said.
Earlier this year Comoros President Mohamed Taki banned the sale of alcoholic drinks, but exempted sales to foreign tourists staying in hotels.
Soldiers recently seized and destroyed alcoholic drinks after traders had been warned not to sell them, residents said.

Taki, elected last year, has taken a tough line in enforcing Islamic standards in the federal Islamic republic's estimated 500,000 population. Islam is the official religion and 99 percent of the population are Moslems.
